boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named NDSU spaces documented through university sources for studying, meeting, recreation, making, and taking a campus break.

cards.title: Set up by Sugihara Hall’s big windows
cards.subtitle: Second floor · Sugihara Hall
cards.notes: Bring a solo task or a small group session to the second-floor seating, then choose a window-side spot for natural light.
cards.short_summary: A student-nominated second-floor study setting with varied seating and large windows.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU’s student feature documents the second floor of Sugihara Hall as having seating for groups or individuals and large windows with natural light.
cards.source_title: Students share their favorite spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Located inside Sugihara Hall; use during building access hours.

cards.title: Use the Union as a campus-meetup base
cards.subtitle: 1401 Administration Avenue · NDSU campus
cards.notes: Meet a classmate, browse organization tables or posters, and use the shared building as a convenient starting point between classes.

cards.evidence_claim: NDSU identifies Memorial Union as a shared student space for studying, connecting, dining, and engaging; its building page lists Student Engagement and Student Organizations among its occupants.

cards.title: Take a movement break at Wallman
cards.subtitle: Wallman Wellness Center · NDSU campus

cards.evidence_claim: NDSU documents that Wallman Wellness Center includes fitness equipment, a climbing wall, courts, a track, and an aquatic facility; commuter guidance says enrolled students use facilities with an NDSU ID.
cards.access_notes: Student-fee-supported facility; bring NDSU ID and check current facility access before visiting.

cards.title: Pause in the demonstration gardens
cards.subtitle: Horticulture Research and Demonstration Gardens · NDSU campus
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk through the garden area between classes, keeping to designated paths and respecting active research plantings.
cards.short_summary: A named campus garden highlighted by an NDSU student as a place to decompress.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU’s student feature names the Horticulture Research and Demonstration Gardens among a student’s favorite campus places for a break from studying.
cards.source_title: Students share their favorite spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor research and demonstration area; visit respectfully during daylight and follow posted site guidance.

cards.title: Make Churchill Field a fresh-air stop
cards.subtitle: Churchill Field · NDSU campus
cards.notes: Use the field’s surrounding outdoor setting for a short reset between commitments, and give scheduled or reserved activities priority.
cards.short_summary: A named campus outdoor space featured by NDSU in its student-spots story.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU’s student feature includes a campus photograph of Churchill Field while presenting student-selected places for focus and relaxation.
cards.source_title: Students share their favorite spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor event space; availability can change with university programming and weather.

cards.title: Claim a quiet-study room at ACE
cards.subtitle: Lower Level, West Dining Center · ACE
cards.notes: Bring focused coursework to ACE’s quiet-study area; use its computer lab, conference rooms, or quiet rooms as your task requires.
cards.short_summary: A large quiet-study space below West Dining Center with study rooms and academic-support amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU says ACE’s Lower Level of West Dining Center space includes tutoring areas, conference rooms, a computer lab, and ten quiet study rooms.
cards.access_notes: NDSU lists quiet-study hours during the school year as 9 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Thursday and 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Friday; closed weekends and breaks.

cards.title: Use the Main Library beyond the stacks
cards.subtitle: Main Library · NDSU campus
cards.notes: Choose a computer cluster or study area for coursework, then ask library staff about resources or space options for your project.

cards.evidence_claim: NDSU states that the Main Library has computer clusters and fully equipped spaces, including the Digital Fabrication Lab and Multimedia Studio, for student use.
cards.source_title: Campus resources provide a pathway to success

cards.title: Make something in the Digital Fabrication Lab
cards.subtitle: Main Library · NDSU campus
cards.notes: Start with a project idea, then check the lab’s current student-use guidance before bringing files or materials for fabrication work.
cards.short_summary: A specialized Main Library workspace available for students to use.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU identifies the Digital Fabrication Lab as a fully equipped Main Library space available for students to utilize.
cards.source_title: Campus resources provide a pathway to success
cards.access_notes: Located in the Main Library; verify current lab procedures, equipment availability, and any material requirements.

cards.title: Build a media project in the Multimedia Studio
cards.subtitle: Main Library · NDSU campus
cards.notes: Use the studio for a course or creative media task, and confirm current availability or booking steps before planning a group session.
cards.short_summary: A specialized Main Library space NDSU identifies as available for students.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU identifies the Multimedia Studio as a fully equipped space in the Main Library that students can utilize.
cards.source_title: Campus resources provide a pathway to success
cards.access_notes: Located in the Main Library; confirm current studio access and any reservation requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Schedule a game-room study break
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union · NDSU campus
cards.notes: Meet friends for a low-key break in the game room, then return to your work; check the Union’s current access and activity rules first.
cards.short_summary: A named Memorial Union recreation space with billiards documented by NDSU Event Services.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU Event Services lists Thundar’s Game Room among campus venues and provides an image labeled “Thundar’s Game Room Billiards.”
cards.access_notes: Located in Memorial Union; check current Union hours and game-room availability before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented ways NDSU marks Bison identity—from its Friday colors and Homecoming rituals to songs with their own calls and responses.

cards.title: Wear Green and Yellow on Friday
cards.subtitle: Bison Pride Fridays
cards.notes: On a Friday, wear green and yellow to join the campus-wide Bison Pride tradition; the university explicitly invites students, staff, alumni and fans to take part.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Friday signal of NDSU identity in the school’s green and yellow.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU describes Bison Pride Fridays as a tradition and says wearing green and yellow is a way for students, faculty, staff, alumni and fans to show pride.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: No special access is stated; participate by wearing green and yellow.

cards.title: Come Back for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: NDSU Homecoming, established 1921
cards.notes: Plan around Homecoming week and choose an advertised event such as the parade or game; it is NDSU’s long-running annual reunion-and-spirit tradition.
cards.short_summary: A campus celebration running since 1921, with documented pauses during wartime and 2020.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU says its first Homecoming was held in 1921 and that the tradition has been celebrated annually except in 1943, 1944 and 2020.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Events and access vary by the annual Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Line Up for the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: A signature NDSU Homecoming tradition
cards.notes: Check the current Homecoming schedule for the route, then watch the parade for its student and campus spirit—including the Gold Star Marching Band.
cards.short_summary: The parade is a documented centerpiece of the university’s annual Homecoming observance.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU identifies a parade featuring the Gold Star Marching Band as one of its long-standing Homecoming traditions.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Route, timing and viewing arrangements vary by year; consult the current Homecoming schedule.

cards.entity_name: Blue Key Honor Society Homecoming Performance
cards.title: Catch Blue Key’s Homecoming Performance
cards.subtitle: Part of NDSU Homecoming
cards.notes: Look for the Blue Key Honor Society performance on the current Homecoming program; it is specifically named by NDSU among the week’s enduring rituals.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming performance tied to NDSU’s Blue Key Honor Society.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU lists a performance by the Blue Key Honor Society among the long-standing traditions that mark Homecoming.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Scheduling and attendance details depend on the annual Homecoming program.

cards.title: See the Homecoming Court Crowned
cards.subtitle: NDSU Homecoming Court
cards.notes: Follow the current Homecoming schedule to see when the court is recognized; the crowning is one of the traditions NDSU names as part of its celebration.
cards.short_summary: The formal crowning moment in NDSU’s Homecoming program.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU identifies the crowning of a Homecoming Court as a long-standing tradition of NDSU Homecoming.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Timing and audience access vary by the annual Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Hear the Gold Star Marching Band
cards.subtitle: “The Pride of North Dakota”
cards.notes: Watch for the band at a Bison spirit event or Homecoming parade and listen for its role in carrying NDSU’s music and pageantry forward.
cards.short_summary: NDSU’s century-plus marching-band tradition, formally named Gold Star in 1924.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU says the Gold Star Marching Band has been part of its spirit and tradition for more than a century and received its Gold Star designation in 1924.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Performance locations and access depend on the event schedule.

cards.title: Join the “State Bison” Yell
cards.subtitle: NDSU school song: “We Are The Pride”
cards.notes: Listen to the official recording and learn the callouts before a spirit event; the song includes the distinctive “STATE BISON!” yell and repeated “FIGHT!” calls.
cards.short_summary: An NDSU fight song built around Bison-specific shouted responses.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU publishes “We Are The Pride” as a school song, including the “STATE BISON!” yell and “FIGHT!” calls.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: The official page provides a recording; event use varies by program.

cards.title: Answer “On Bison” with a Yell
cards.subtitle: NDSU school song: “On Bison”
cards.notes: Use the official lyrics to recognize the “State Bison!” and “Fight You Bison!” responses, then listen for the song at Bison spirit occasions.
cards.short_summary: A school song that turns “Bison” into a call-and-response cheer.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU publishes “On Bison” among its school songs and includes the “State Bison!” and “Fight You Bison!” yells in its lyrics.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: The official page provides a recording; event use varies by program.

cards.title: Sing “The Yellow and The Green”
cards.subtitle: NDSU school song by A. E. Minard and C. S. Putnam
cards.notes: Listen through the university’s recording, then notice how the song makes NDSU’s two school colors part of a shared musical ritual.
cards.short_summary: A named NDSU song centered on the university’s green-and-yellow colors.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU lists “The Yellow and The Green,” with words by A. E. Minard and music by C. S. Putnam, among its school songs.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: The official page provides a recording; event use varies by program.

cards.title: Start at the Main Campus Gates
cards.subtitle: First-day-of-class Bison ritual
cards.notes: Make the main gates your first stop on the opening day of classes, then take a photo or continue into campus—an NDSU-published student experience prompt.
cards.short_summary: A first-day campus-marker ritual built around NDSU’s main gates.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU’s official pre-graduation experience list specifically tells students to walk through the main campus gates to kick off their first day of class.
cards.source_title: Top things to do before you graduate from NDSU
cards.access_notes: The source frames this as a first-day activity; enter campus in accordance with posted access rules.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at North Dakota State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend route through NDSU’s campus hub, galleries, study spaces, and student recreation—ending with a downtown campus gallery visit.

cards.title: Start at the Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: Campus hub · NDSU
cards.notes: Begin by getting oriented in the Union, then use its posted building information to locate student services, dining, recreation, and the gallery.
cards.short_summary: A practical starting point for seeing several student-facing campus spaces in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU identifies the Memorial Union as home to student services, dining, Thundar’s Game Room, and an art gallery.
cards.source_title: What's in the MU | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Check the Memorial Union’s current building hours before going; services and spaces may have separate schedules.

cards.title: Find the Zip to Zap portal
cards.subtitle: First floor, Memorial Union · NDSU Museum and Collections
cards.notes: While in the Union, look for the museum portal on the first floor and pause to read the display as an introduction to NDSU collections.
cards.short_summary: A named NDSU Museum and Collections portal located inside the Memorial Union.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU Museum and Collections lists Zip to Zap on the first floor of the Memorial Union.
cards.access_notes: Located on the Memorial Union’s first floor; verify building access before visiting.

cards.title: Take in the Memorial Union Gallery
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Memorial Union · NDSU Museum and Collections
cards.notes: Go upstairs to view the current exhibition, then note the artist and exhibition details for a conversation starter with a new classmate.
cards.short_summary: A rotating campus gallery presenting visiting artists, collection works, and student work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Union Gallery is on the second floor and hosts twelve exhibitions each year, including visiting artists and student work.
cards.source_title: NDSU Galleries | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: NDSU lists academic-year gallery hours as Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Make a game-room plan
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Memorial Union · NDSU
cards.notes: Head downstairs to see the bowling lanes, billiards, table tennis, shuffleboard, foosball, and air hockey, then choose an activity for later.
cards.short_summary: A named Memorial Union recreation space with bowling, table games, and student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Thundar’s Game Room is in the Memorial Union’s lower level and includes bowling lanes, pool tables, table tennis, shuffleboard, foosball, and air hockey.
cards.source_title: Thundar's Game Room | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: NDSU lists academic-year hours through midnight on Friday and Saturday; activities may have hourly rates or specials.

cards.title: Settle into the Main Library
cards.subtitle: NDSU Libraries · Campus
cards.notes: Use the library’s study areas to make a simple weekend plan, find a group workspace, or ask at a service desk about research support.
cards.short_summary: NDSU’s principal library offers individual and group study options alongside student support services.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU reports that the Main Library has reservable study rooms, quiet areas, group workspaces, computer clusters, and conference rooms.
cards.access_notes: Library access and study-room availability vary by term and time; check current library hours and reservation rules.

cards.title: Spot the library-lobby portal
cards.subtitle: Library lobby · NDSU Museum and Collections
cards.notes: Before leaving the library, find this named museum portal in the lobby and use its display as a short, self-guided science stop.
cards.short_summary: A named museum portal located in the NDSU Library lobby.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU Museum and Collections lists How Do Hybrids Happen? in the lobby of the Library.
cards.access_notes: Located in the library lobby; confirm Main Library access hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Scene, Through the Eyes of Another
cards.title: Continue to A. Glenn Hill Center
cards.subtitle: Main floor, A. Glenn Hill Center · NDSU Museum and Collections
cards.notes: Make this a short campus walk: locate the main-floor portal, read the interpretive material, and photograph only where campus rules allow.
cards.short_summary: A named NDSU Museum and Collections portal in the A. Glenn Hill Center.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU Museum and Collections lists Scene, Through the Eyes of Another on the main floor of the A. Glenn Hill Center.
cards.access_notes: Located on the main floor of A. Glenn Hill Center; follow building access rules.

cards.entity_name: Have You Ever Dated a Tree?
cards.title: Stop by Barry Hall’s tree portal
cards.subtitle: Main floor, Barry Hall · NDSU Museum and Collections
cards.notes: Walk to Barry Hall and find this named display on the main floor; use it as a reason to explore a different part of campus together.
cards.short_summary: A named museum portal in Barry Hall focused on a distinct collection display.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU Museum and Collections lists Have You Ever Dated a Tree? on the main floor of Barry Hall.
cards.access_notes: Located on Barry Hall’s main floor; confirm building access before visiting.

cards.title: Visit the President’s Gallery
cards.subtitle: Beside the President’s Office, Old Main · NDSU
cards.notes: In Old Main, look beside the President’s Office for the gallery and spend time with its student-focused exhibition before heading downtown.
cards.short_summary: An Old Main gallery presenting NDSU’s values, research, mission, and student-centered exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU states that the President’s Gallery is beside the President’s Office in Old Main and presents two student-focused exhibitions annually.
cards.source_title: NDSU Galleries | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: NDSU lists visits Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. during the academic year; verify current access before going.

cards.title: Finish at Flakoll Gallery downtown
cards.subtitle: Renaissance Hall, downtown Fargo · NDSU Museum and Collections
cards.notes: End the route at NDSU’s downtown gallery in Renaissance Hall, where exhibitions connect art, architecture, student projects, and visiting artists.
cards.short_summary: A downtown NDSU gallery in Renaissance Hall with recurring exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: NDSU states that Flakoll Gallery is located downtown in Renaissance Hall and hosts exhibitions featuring alumni, faculty, students, and visiting artists.
cards.source_title: NDSU Galleries | North Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Located in Renaissance Hall downtown; review the School of Design, Architecture and Art’s current exhibition information before visiting.
